title: 5 Trends for 2019
notes: TrendWatching Quarterly, November 2018 issue (URL path quarterly/2018-11; earliest 200 capture found is 2018-12-19). Labels from the numbered overview (printed with a trailing full stop, dropped here). The 2019 Trend Report (Premium, 100+ insights) is not captured. target_year 2019 from the title.

entries.label: LEGISLATIVE BRANDS
entries.quote: In 2019, frustrated consumers will welcome LEGISLATIVE BRANDS: corporate interests using their significant power to call for, promote, and even impose laws that drive constructive change and make the world a better place.
entries.subject: Brands lobbying for or imposing pro-social rules
entries.note: Dek: 'Progressive consumers will welcome the 'law of the brand'.'

entries.label: LAB RATS
entries.quote: In 2019, LAB RATS will see human wellness and lifestyle as an engineering problem to be solved.
entries.subject: Self-experimentation and biohacking for wellness
entries.note: Dek: 'Why an extreme test and fix mindset is the future of wellness.'

entries.label: OPEN SOURCE SOLUTIONS
entries.quote: That’s why in 2019, the boldest and most inspiring organizations will embrace OPEN SOURCE SOLUTIONS: sharing and even giving away their innovative solutions to our toughest shared problems.
entries.subject: Companies open-sourcing sustainability solutions
entries.note: Dek: 'A bold new frontier for sustainability.'

entries.label: SUPERHUMAN RESOURCES
entries.quote: In 2019, rising numbers of consumers will demand SUPERHUMAN RESOURCES: ethical AI and algorithms that deliver fair and unbiased decisions.
entries.subject: Ethical, unbiased AI
entries.note: Dek: 'It's time for our emerging AI overlords to play fair.'

entries.label: FANTASY IRL
entries.quote: Yes, 24/7 connectivity and digital experiences that blur the boundaries of the real and virtual are not 'new' trends, but in 2019 their convergence will reach deeper than ever before into culture.
entries.subject: Blending imagined and real worlds (gaming, AR, immersive play)
entries.note: Dek: 'Imagined and real worlds collide in the name of play.'
